body:
# Lindos From Rhodes Town: Bus, Boat or Tour?

**Short answer:** take the public bus if Lindos itself is what you want to see.

Choose an organized transfer if you want the simplicity of hotel pickup and a fixed return.

Choose a boat if the journey — coastline, swimming stops and approaching Lindos from the sea — is part of what you want from the day.

These are not three versions of the same trip.

They create three quite different days.

## Start with one question: do you want Lindos or a day trip built around Lindos?

This is the easiest way to decide.

If your priority is:

the village,

the Acropolis,

lunch,

wandering the lanes,

and perhaps some beach time,

then getting there efficiently makes sense.

That points toward the bus or an organized road transfer.

If the idea of cruising down Rhodes' east coast, swimming in clear bays and arriving at Lindos from the water sounds as important as Lindos itself, take the boat.

Do not book a boat simply because it looks more romantic in the photos.

You usually give up some time in Lindos in exchange for the sea journey.

## The public bus is the simplest independent option

KTEL Rhodes runs regular services between Rhodes Town and Lindos.

Services leave from the Rhodes Town bus network around Mandraki and operate multiple times per day during the main season.

The important advantage is freedom.

You are not joining an excursion.

You choose your outward bus.

You choose your return.

Once you reach Lindos, the day is yours.

There is no swim-stop schedule and nobody is waiting for twenty other passengers to get back on a coach.

If I wanted to explore Lindos properly, this would be my default starting point.

## What the bus gives you that a tour does not

Time.

That sounds obvious, but it matters.

Lindos is more than the Acropolis.

The village itself is worth wandering.

There are narrow whitewashed lanes, rooftop restaurants, shops, old captain's houses, Lindos Beach and St Paul's Bay nearby.

And the Acropolis visit takes time too.

If you arrive independently, you can decide that you have had enough after three hours.

Or stay much longer.

A fixed excursion cannot give you that freedom.

## The Acropolis ticket is separate

Whatever transport you choose, do not assume the Acropolis of Lindos is included.

The official full-price admission is currently **€20**.

That is separate from most transport and boat tickets.

So when comparing options, add the entrance fee where necessary.

A cheap transport offer with a €20 Acropolis ticket added may still be excellent value.

But it should be compared honestly with tours that include more services.

## When I would choose the bus

I would use public transport if:

* Lindos itself is the main goal
* I want plenty of free time
* I want to visit the Acropolis without rushing
* I would like a long lunch
* I am comfortable finding the bus stop myself
* hotel pickup is not important
* I want to keep the day inexpensive

For one or two independent travellers staying in Rhodes Town, it is hard to beat.

## The organized road transfer is not really a tour

This distinction matters.

There are products sold as Lindos excursions that are basically:

**hotel pickup → air-conditioned transfer → four hours free in Lindos → return.**

And that can be excellent.

You are not paying someone to march you around the village with a flag.

You are paying to remove transportation from the problem.

One current excursion picks up from Rhodes Town, Ixia, Ialyssos, Kallithea and some nearby areas, stops briefly at the Lindos viewpoint and then gives approximately **four hours of free time** in the village.

The Acropolis ticket is extra.

That is a very sensible product for someone who wants independence after arrival but does not want to learn the bus system.

## My easy road option

A current Viator transfer gives you roughly four hours in Lindos and handles pickup and return from several resort areas.

There is no compulsory guided programme once you arrive.

You can visit the Acropolis, have lunch, shop or go to the beach.



[From Rhodes: Easy Morning Transfer to Lindos & 4 Hours Free Time](https://www.viator.com/tours/Rhodes/Lindos-Half-Day-Express-Bus-Tour/d4272-49323P1?pid=P00320497&mcid=42383&medium=link&medium_version=selector "affiliate-button")

I would choose this over the public bus if **door-to-door convenience** mattered more than saving money.

For a couple already staying in Rhodes Town, I would still compare the bus first.

## Boat is a completely different experience

Going to Lindos by sea solves a different problem.

You are no longer asking:

**What is the easiest way to get to Lindos?**

You are asking:

**How can I turn Lindos into a boat day?**

That can include coastal views, swimming and time on deck before or after the village.

And Lindos really does look different from the water.

The Acropolis sits above the white village and bays in a way that makes the geography much easier to understand.

The trade-off is time.

## A fast boat can still give you serious Lindos time

Not every boat means spending the whole day crawling down the coast.

One current high-speed service leaves from Mandraki Harbour in Rhodes Town and offers around **four hours in Lindos** on one booking option.

Another version reduces the Lindos stop to about three hours and adds a swim stop at Tsambika.

That is a useful choice because it exposes the trade-off very clearly.

More swimming means less Lindos.

Neither version is inherently better.

## My boat pick from Rhodes Town

The current **High-Speed Boat to Lindos** leaves from Mandraki and gives you a choice between a longer independent stop in Lindos or a version with an additional swimming stop.



[High Speed Cruise to Lindos with 4 hours of Free Time](https://www.viator.com/tours/Rhodes/High-Speed-Boat-to-Lindos/d4272-91578P1?pid=P00320497&mcid=42383&medium=link&medium_version=selector "affiliate-button")

I would choose it if approaching Lindos from the sea appealed to me and I still wanted meaningful time in the village.

It is much closer to “transport by sea” than a giant all-day sightseeing cruise.

## The classic full-day cruise is about the coast

There is another kind of Lindos boat trip.

It sails slowly down the east coast, stops to swim and gives you a shorter period in Lindos.

For example, one current cruise from Faliraki lasts around **7.5 hours**, stops at Tsambika Beach and Anthony Quinn Bay, and gives roughly **three hours in Lindos**.

That is a good product.

But it is important to understand what you are buying.

The attraction is:

**coast + swimming + Lindos.**

Not maximum time at the Acropolis.

## If swimming is half the reason for going

A current cruise from Faliraki includes:

* around three hours in Lindos
* a swimming stop at Tsambika
* a swimming stop at Anthony Quinn Bay
* shaded seating onboard



[Faliraki: Lindos Boat Cruise with Swim stops & Free Time](https://www.viator.com/tours/Rhodes/Lindos-Boat-Cruise-from-Faliraki-with-Swim-Stops/d4272-5583275P2?pid=P00320497&mcid=42383&medium=link&medium_version=selector "affiliate-button")

I would choose this if I wanted a **Rhodes east-coast boat day that happens to include Lindos**.

I would not choose it if Lindos was my main archaeological sightseeing day.

## Watch the group size on boat cruises

This is another place where the photographs can be misleading.

A boat can look relaxed and spacious when photographed without passengers.

Then the listing says maximum 80.

Or 200.

One current Rhodes Town Lindos cruise is listed with a maximum of **280 travellers**.

Another large vessel lists up to **245**.

That does not make them bad.

Large sightseeing boats can be fun.

They also tend to be affordable and have more onboard facilities.

But this is not the same experience as a small excursion boat.

If crowd level matters to you, look for the actual maximum passenger count.

Do not rely on the words:

**comfortable**

**relaxing**

or

**premium**.

## Bus vs organized transfer

These two are much closer competitors than bus vs boat.

### Choose the bus if…

You want the cheapest straightforward option.

You are staying in Rhodes Town.

You are comfortable checking timetables.

You want to control when you return.

### Choose organized transfer if…

You want pickup close to your hotel.

You do not want to think about bus stops.

You are staying in Ixia, Ialyssos or another pickup zone.

Four hours in Lindos sounds about right.

The difference is mostly convenience.

Not sightseeing quality.

## Bus vs boat

This is a much easier distinction.

### Bus

You travel inland.

The journey is transportation.

Most of the value is at Lindos.

### Boat

The journey is part of the excursion.

You see Rhodes from the sea.

You may swim.

You sacrifice some time in Lindos.

So the question is not which is objectively better.

It is:

**Where do you want to spend the hours?**

## How much time do you really need in Lindos?

I would think about it like this.

### Around 2 hours

Enough for a quick look around the village or an Acropolis-focused visit.

Not enough for everything comfortably.

### Around 3 hours

Reasonable for Acropolis + village if you keep moving.

Or village + lunch without much archaeology.

### Around 4 hours

Much more comfortable.

Acropolis, village, lunch or a little beach time can fit without constantly checking the clock.

### Five hours or more

This is where independent travel begins to shine.

You can stop treating Lindos as an attraction and spend part of the day simply being there.

## Do not underestimate the climb

Getting to Lindos is the easy part.

Getting up to the Acropolis is another question.

The site sits above the village, and reaching it involves climbing through steep pedestrian lanes and steps.

In hot weather, that can become the physically hardest part of the day.

The official site itself describes the archaeological area as being reached on foot from the traditional settlement.

So if someone in your group struggles with steep climbs, heat or prolonged walking, transport from Rhodes is only half the planning problem.

We will deal with that separately in:

**Can You Visit Lindos If You Hate Steep Climbs?**

## Booking trap #1: the Acropolis ticket is not included

This comes up repeatedly.

A Lindos transfer may describe the Acropolis as one of the things you can see.

That does not mean admission is included.

The official ticket is currently €20.

Check before comparing total costs.

## Booking trap #2: “Lindos boat trip” may mean only two or three hours in Lindos

Read the itinerary.

Some tours spend more of the day cruising and swimming than actually visiting Lindos.

That may be exactly what you want.

But it should not be a surprise.

## Booking trap #3: starting in Faliraki is not starting in Rhodes Town

A lot of attractive Lindos cruises depart from **Faliraki**, not central Rhodes Town.

That matters if your hotel is in Rhodes Town.

You need to include the trip to Faliraki unless transfer is included.

A slightly less glamorous boat leaving from Mandraki may therefore be much easier.

## Booking trap #4: hotel pickup has boundaries

“Pickup offered” does not mean every hotel on Rhodes.

Tour operators normally define particular resort zones.

Rhodes is a large island.

A pickup covering Ixia and Ialyssos may not cover Kiotari or Lindos.

Check the actual hotel list before treating transport as included.

## Booking trap #5: do not book private just because it sounds better

Private Lindos tours are widely available.

They can make sense for:

* families
* four or more people sharing the cost
* cruise passengers with a fixed return deadline
* people combining Lindos with other Rhodes sights
* travellers who want complete control over timing

But private does not make the Acropolis flatter.

And it does not automatically include its entrance ticket.

One current private Rhodes/Lindos tour specifically lists the Acropolis admission as an additional €20 per person.

Private buys flexibility.

Not magical access.

## Which would I choose?

### Staying in Rhodes Town and mainly want Lindos

**Public bus.**

Simple, inexpensive and maximum independence.

### Want zero transport hassle

**Organized road transfer with four hours free.**

Especially attractive from Ixia or Ialyssos.

### Want Lindos but hate bus journeys

**High-speed boat from Mandraki.**

You still get useful time in Lindos while making the journey part of the experience.

### Want swimming and a boat day

**Full-day cruise.**

Think Anthony Quinn Bay, Tsambika and Lindos together.

### Love archaeology

**Road, not cruise.**

Give Lindos as much time as possible.

### Travelling with children who care more about swimming than ruins

**Boat.**

Three hours in Lindos may be plenty.

### Hate fixed schedules

**Public bus.**

Assuming the timetable works for your day.

## Dan's recommendation

I have not taken these particular Lindos excursions myself.

I compared the official transport and archaeological information with current tour itineraries because “day trip to Lindos” can hide three completely different products.

For most independent travellers staying in Rhodes Town, I would start with the bus.

It is hard to justify paying much more merely to sit in another road vehicle.

I would pay extra for an organized transfer if hotel pickup made the day genuinely easier.

And I would pay extra for a boat if I specifically wanted the sea.

That is the important distinction.

**Do not choose the boat because it is a prettier way to reach Lindos.**

Choose it because you want a boat day.

If Lindos itself is the star, spend your time in Lindos.

If the coast is part of the attraction, arrive from the water.

*Some links on this page are affiliate links. If you book through them, I may earn a commission at no extra cost to you.*

**Checked: 27 October 2026.**

subtitle: Bus, organized transfer or boat? The best way to visit Lindos from Rhodes Town depends on whether you want maximum time in the village, an easy hotel-to-hotel day or a cruise with swimming stops.
title: Lindos From Rhodes Town: Bus, Boat or Tour?
